Problem: Let \( F_1 \) and \( F_2 \) be the foci of the ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1\). Point \( P \) is on the ellipse and satisfies \(\left|P F_1\right|:\left|P F_2\right| = 2:1\). Find the area of triangle \( \triangle P F_1 F_2\).

<reflection>
Ellipse equation: \(\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1\), so \(a=3\), \(b=2\). Focal distance \(c=\sqrt{a^2-b^2}=\sqrt{5}\), so the foci are at \((\pm\sqrt{5},0)\). For \(P\) on the ellipse, \(PF_1+PF_2=2a=6\). Given \(|PF_1|:|PF_2|=2:1\), setting \(|PF_1|=2k\), \(|PF_2|=k\) gives \(3k=6\), so \(|PF_1|=4\) and \(|PF_2|=2\). Choosing \(F_1=(\sqrt{5},0)\) and \(F_2=(-\sqrt{5},0)\) is consistent with the foci.
This equation is not the ellipse equation. It is a circle centered at \(F_1\) with radius 3. The ellipse equation is \(\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1\).
Use the correct ellipse equation \(\frac{x^2}{9}+\frac{y^2}{4}=1\) together with the distance equations from \(|PF_1|=4\) and \(|PF_2|=2\) to solve for \(P\).
</reflection>
